content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define nanoparticles and explain their size range
Compare nanoparticles with bulk materials and fine particles
Calculate surface area to volume ratio
Describe uses and potential risks of nanoparticles

are tiny particles between 1 and 100 nanometres in size. At this scale, materials can have very different properties from their bulk form. Nanotechnology is a rapidly growing field with applications in medicine, electronics, and materials science.

A nanoparticle contains a few hundred to a few thousand atoms

The same properties that make nanoparticles useful also raise concerns:
Nanoparticles can pass through skin and cell membranes
Long-term health effects still being studied
More research is needed before nanoparticles are used more widely.
A cube has sides of 2 cm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio.
What would happen to this ratio if the cube was divided into smaller cubes?
The surface area to volume ratio would increase, because smaller particles have relatively more surface area.

State the size range of nanoparticles. (1 mark)
Explain why nanoparticles have a high surface area to volume ratio. (2 marks)
A cube has sides of 3 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio. (3 marks)

Discuss the potential risks of using nanoparticles in everyday products like sunscreen. (4 marks)
